card.name: Subject right before a past-tense verb
card.fires_on: The last word of a subject (a noun, pronoun or relative word) in general web text, just where a past-tense verb such as was, did or included should come next. It is often a past event, such as a law, an election or an experiment.

modes.label: Subject before was
modes.description: A noun phrase about a past event or law, with was expected next.
modes.example: the repeal of the Glass Steagall Act in the 90’s<< was>> a major contributor to the debacle of

modes.label: Pronoun before did
modes.description: you or they in instructions or reflections, followed by a past action verb.
modes.example: Explain what<< you>> did clearly enough for other people to follow

modes.label: Noun before past verb
modes.description: A noun or year naming a past thing, with a past verb coming next.
modes.example: the 2008<< elections>> included the most diverse electorate in U.S

card.writes: It boosts past-tense verbs like was, were, did and gave, and suppresses present-tense verbs like begins, becomes and gets.
card.plain: It marks the spot where the sentence's subject has just ended and a past-tense verb is about to come.
